items.descriptionTR: Plus de 1,2 million de fidèles ont envahi les rues du centre de Madrid dimanche pour une messe célébrée par Léon XIV, au cours de laquelle le pape a appelé à un renouveau de la foi catholique en Espagne.
items.titleTR: VIDÉO. 1,2 million de fidèles pour la messe du pape à Madrid

items.descriptionTR: Huge crowds welcomed Pope Leo XIV to Madrid on Sunday. The pontiff is on a five-day trip around Spain during which he is meeting vulnerable people such as migrants and the homeless, and promoting "genuine human values."
items.titleTR: Pope Leo in Spain: More than a million line Madrid streets

items.descriptionTR: More than a million people filled the streets near one of Madrid's main squares to join Pope Leo for an outdoor Mass.
items.titleTR: Pope Leo tells 1.2m crowd that God stands with the poor

items.descriptionTR: Pope Leo XIV has begun a weeklong visit to Spain, bringing the American pontiff to one of Europe’s historic centres of Christianity at a moment of political tension, social change and renewed curiosity about faith.
items.titleTR: Pope Leo XIV visits Spain as Church seeks a fresh voice in changing Europe

items.descriptionTR: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Spain on Saturday for a seven-day trip focused in part on migration, including a visit to the Canary Islands where he will honour thousands of migrants who died trying to reach Europe. Leo is also scheduled to meet with victims of sex abuse by Catholic clergy, which some 200,000 minors are estimated to have suffered in Spain since 1940.
items.titleTR: Pope Leo visits Spain to highlight migration, meet victims of sexual abuse by clergy

items.descriptionTR: Le souverain pontife a rassemblé plus d’1 million d’Espagnols ce dimanche 7 juin dans la capitale, pour une messe puis une procession, durant laquelle il a fustigé ceux «qui méprisent les hommes». Dans les prochains jours, il devrait s’exprimer sur la question migratoire.
items.titleTR: A Madrid, la foule, la chaleur et la ferveur pour le pape Léon XIV

items.descriptionTR: Selon les conclusions d’une enquête préliminaire, un soldat israélien a ouvert le feu, samedi à Hébron, sur la voiture à bord de laquelle se trouvait l’enfant, lorsqu’elle a accéléré en direction d’un détachement militaire.
items.titleTR: L’armée israélienne ouvre une enquête après la mort d’un bébé palestinien tué par un de ses soldats en Cisjordanie

items.descriptionTR: A seven-month-old baby was laid to rest in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, a day after he was shot dead and his parents were injured by Israeli forces near Hebron, according to family members who witnessed the shooting and the Palestinian Health Ministry.
items.titleTR: Seven-month-old boy killed by Israeli forces laid to rest

items.descriptionTR: Le président n’a pas apprécié des questions posées par la journaliste Kristen Welker, notamment, sur l’Iran et le fonds « anti-instrumentalisation ». Des problèmes liés à la météo ont ajouté des difficultés à l’entretien, que Donald Trump a fini par interrompre brutalement.
items.titleTR: « Vous êtes une chaîne biaisée et malhonnête. Désolé, on arrête là » : une interview de Donald Trump accordée à la chaîne NBC dégénère

items.descriptionTR: Réalisé dans une ferme et sous une pluie battante, l’entretien s’est déroulé dans des conditions improbables. Jusqu’à cette sortie du président américain agacé par des questions sur l’Iran.
items.titleTR: «Vous êtes soit corrompue, soit débile» : Trump met fin à une interview en insultant la journaliste

items.descriptionTR: Plus tôt dimanche, Téhéran avait menacé de frapper les intérêts américains et israéliens au Moyen-Orient, en représailles aux attaques menées dans la journée par l’Etat hébreu sur la banlieue sud de Beyrouth, bastion du Hezbollah pro-iranien. « L’armée de l’air a jusqu’à présent intercepté l’ensemble des missiles tirés depuis l’Iran », a précisé un communiqué militaire israélien.
items.titleTR: EN DIRECT, Moyen-Orient : Israël annonce être la cible de missiles iraniens, pour la première fois depuis le cessez-le-feu annoncé le 8 avril

items.descriptionTR: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said that a missile attack on Israel was a "warning" after the Israeli strike on Beirut earlier in the day, threatening wider strikes in the event of new aggression.
items.titleTR: Iran targets Israel in 'warning' over Beirut attack

items.descriptionTR: Deux personnes ont été tuées ce dimanche par des frappes israéliennes dans la banlieue sud de la capitale libanaise. Selon l’armée israélienne, l’Iran a effectué des tirs de missiles vers son territoire.
items.titleTR: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : Israël annonce la fermeture des écoles lundi après des tirs de missiles iraniens, les premiers depuis le cessez-le-feu du 8 avril

items.descriptionTR: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called a Russian attack on a nuclear storage facility near Chernobyl "vile." The UN's nuclear watchdog said no increased radiation had been registered at the site.
items.titleTR: Ukraine: Russian drone hits nuclear-fuel storage facility

items.descriptionTR: Russian forces deliberately struck a storage facility for spent nuclear fuel near Ukraine's Chornobyl power plant, Volodymyr Zelensky said.
items.titleTR: Russia hits nuclear fuel storage facility near Chornobyl

items.descriptionTR: Close to the front line in southern Ukraine, Zaporizhzhia is the biggest nuclear power plant in Europe.
items.titleTR: Drone Hits Captured Nuclear Plant in Ukraine – IAEA

items.descriptionTR: Quatre personnes ont été tuées en Ukraine par des attaques de drones. Ce dimanche 7 juin, le président ukrainien rencontre Emmanuel Macron, Friedrich Merz et Keir Starmer.
items.titleTR: Frappe russe sur un site de stockage de combustible nucléaire en Ukraine, Zelensky dénonce un acte d’une «lâcheté absolue»

items.descriptionTR: Sunday's election in Kosovo — the third in under 16 months — is marked by a clash between former allies PM Albin Kurti and ex-President Vjosa Osmani, deadlock in the dialogue with Serbia, and obstacles to EU integration.
items.titleTR: Successive elections take a hit on Kosovo's coffers

items.descriptionTR: Kosovans began voting on Sunday in another snap election, the country’s third in just over a year, as mounting frustration over political deadlock tests the patience of voters in Europe’s youngest state.
items.titleTR: Kosovo votes again in snap election as frustration grows over political gridlock

items.descriptionTR: "Enough is Enough", the words of Gezim Selimi, a retired teacher in Pristina as he voted today in the Kosovo elections. He was one of a snap shot of voters questioned by journalists about what it like to be voting again in Kosovo.
items.titleTR: Kosovo: Former President warns of the cost of political deadlock

items.descriptionTR: Armenians have voted in elections that pit pro-EU Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan against the pro-Russia opposition. Peace efforts with longtime foe Azerbaijan are also a main election issue.
items.titleTR: Armenia votes in election with Russia and EU looking on

items.descriptionTR: In the weeks before the vote, Russia banned the import of several products from Armenia — seen as a move to heap economic pressure on the country.
items.titleTR: Armenia Votes in Test of PM’s Pivot Away From Russia

items.descriptionTR: As Armenians vote in a parliamentary election seen as a test of Nikol Pashinyan’s pro-Western course, RFI asks two regional experts what the result could mean for peace with Azerbaijan and relations with Russia.
items.titleTR: Armenia election: what the vote could mean for Russia, the West and Azerbaijan

items.descriptionTR: One ballot box, two competing battles. In Armenia, voters are heading to the polls to decide the future direction of their country. But beneath the political campaigns lies a far more insidious warfare. Analysts warn that a massive, coordinated network of foreign disinformation - much of it tracing back to Russia - is systematically weaponizing the deep-seated trauma of recent wars. FRANCE 24's Olivia Bizot reports from Yerevan.
items.titleTR: Massive disinformation campaign underway in Armenia ahead of elections, analysts warn

items.descriptionTR: Authorities said two of the victims are in critical condition after a gunfire near Toledo's Old West End Festival, with suspects still on the run.
items.titleTR: US: 12 injured after shooting near festival in Ohio, police hunt suspects

items.descriptionTR: A shootout near a community festival in Ohio left at least 12 people wounded by gunfire, with no suspects in custody, police said.
items.titleTR: Manhunt after 12 wounded in shooting near US festival

items.descriptionTR: La plupart des victimes sont âgées d’environ 20 ans. La police recherche toujours les tireurs.
items.titleTR: Etats-Unis : dans l’Ohio, des tirs font 12 blessés en marge d’une fête locale

items.descriptionTR: The Iranian-born author of the acclaimed graphic novel and film offered a deeply personal account of Iran's Islamic Revolution.
items.titleTR: Marjane Satrapi, author of 'Persepolis,' dies at 56

items.descriptionTR: Franco-Iranian author and film director Marjane Satrapi, best known for the graphic novel and film Persepolis, has died aged 56.
items.titleTR: Marjane Satrapi, French-Iranian author of 'Persepolis', dies aged 56

items.descriptionTR: Donald Trump's son-in-law is linked to a megaproject on Albania's protected coast that has triggered protests and EU scrutiny over risks to flamingos and endangered habitats.
items.titleTR: Kushner-backed Albania resort sparks protests, EU concerns

items.descriptionTR: Thursday marked the fourth consecutive day of protests in Albania, sparked by plans for a proposed billion-dollar luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner, the husband of Donald Trump's daughter, Ivanka Trump. Online, however, misleading videos of the unrest are going viral, with social media users sharing old and out-of-context footage falsely presented as scenes from the current demonstrations. Many protesters fear that the Kushner-backed development could devastate a protected wildlife ecosystem.
items.titleTR: False videos swirl as Albania protests Kushner resort plan

items.descriptionTR: Derrière la défense d’une zone protégée et la contestation d’un mégaprojet porté par Jared Kushner et Ivanka Trump, des manifestants dénoncent, depuis le 1er juin à Tirana, un système rongé par la corruption, au service des intérêts d’une petite oligarchie.
items.titleTR: En Albanie, le projet touristique à plusieurs milliards d’euros de la famille Trump fait exploser la colère sociale

items.descriptionTR: Protesters have clashed with police in Southampton over the December murder of finance student Henry Nowak. The fatally injured victim was handcuffed by police after his killer accused him of racist abuse.
items.titleTR: UK: Protest erupts over student murder

items.descriptionTR: Former UK Labour Party leader Jeremy Corbyn has called on people to ignore the comments of US Vice President JD Vance over the death of 18-year-old Henry Nowak and listen to his father Mark Nowak's calls for calm instead.
items.titleTR: Corbyn urges people to ignore JD Vance's Nowak comments

items.descriptionTR: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer 's office on Friday condemned comments by US Vice President JD Vance, who blamed immigration for the death of a university student who was handcuffed as he lay dying from a stab wound.
items.titleTR: UK PM criticises Vance over comments about teen's stabbing death

items.titleTR: Malta votes in snap parliamentary election

items.titleTR: Kosovo votes again in snap election as frustration grows over political gridlock

items.descriptionTR: Reforms under new Prime Minister Peter Magyar will enable the EU to free up billions in frozen assistance for Budapest. The EU's Ursula von der Leyen announced the news as Magyar visited Brussels.
items.titleTR: EU unblocks €16 billion in Hungary assistance as Magyar promises reforms

items.descriptionTR: Hungary’s Prime Minister Peter Magyar will meet European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels on Friday in his first top-level talks with EU leaders since his election victory in April, as he seeks to unlock billions of euros in frozen EU funds.
items.titleTR: Hungarian PM Peter Magyar seeks release of frozen EU funds in Brussels talks

items.descriptionTR: More than a million people have been forced to flee their homes in southern Lebanon due to fighting between Israeli forces and Hezbollah. As many shelter in Beirut stadiums, sport is sometimes a welcome distraction.
items.titleTR: Sport helping displaced Lebanese living in stadium to cope

items.descriptionTR: Israel's war in southern Lebanon is reopening old wounds far beyond the battlefield. More than a million people have been displaced since Israel and Hezbollah returned to full-scale conflict in March, while political leaders remain split over the powerful Shiite movement and negotiations with Israel. As calls for federalism and even partition become louder, the war is reviving debate over Lebanon's political system, national identity and territorial unity.
items.titleTR: Lebanon war reopens old divisions as fears grow for country's unity

items.descriptionTR: The Israeli military has vowed to press ahead with its military campaign in Lebanon and said it would step up operations against Hezbollah.
items.titleTR: Israeli military vows to 'intensify' Lebanon operation

items.descriptionTR: France has requested an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council after Israeli forces seized the medieval Beaufort castle in Lebanon, the French foreign minister said Sunday.
items.titleTR: France requests emergency UN meeting amid Israeli advance in Lebanon

items.titleTR: Russia claims over 300 drones intercepted and destroyed

items.descriptionTR: Russia’s Defense Ministry claimed it had targeted defense production plants and transportation infrastructure used by Ukraine’s military.
items.titleTR: At Least 21 Killed in Russian Strikes Across Ukraine

items.titleTR: Moscow to Host U.S.-Russia Hockey Match Next Month

items.descriptionTR: Russia-U.S. talks on economic and energy issues continue despite a pause in Ukraine peace negotiations, Putin's special envoy Kirill Dmitriev told Reuters on Thursday, ‌adding he spoke to U.S. counterparts a day earlier. He spoke on the sidelines of the St Petersburg economic summit, where, as FRANCE 24's international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert explains, a veritable 'rogues' gallery' of notorious figures showed up in support of Putin's policies.
items.titleTR: A 'rogues' gallery' of notorious figures at Russia's biggest economic conference

items.descriptionTR: « La ligne de contact actuelle doit servir de point de départ aux négociations. Les frontières internationales ne doivent pas être modifiées par la force », ont également déclaré Emmanuel Macron, Friedrich Merz et Keir Starmer, dans un communiqué commun avec le président ukrainien. Les dirigeants français, allemand et ukrainien étaient reçus à Londres par le premier ministre britannique.
items.titleTR: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la France, l’Allemagne et le Royaume-Uni soutiennent la proposition de Volodymyr Zelensky d’un « dialogue direct » entre Kiev et Moscou

items.descriptionTR: Russian President Vladimir Putin has said that he sees "no point" in meeting his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky until a peace deal is ready.
items.titleTR: 'No point' in meeting Zelensky before peace deal - Putin

items.descriptionTR: Putin has said he would only meet Zelensky to finalize an already agreed deal, rejecting calls to meet before then.
items.titleTR: In Open Letter to Putin, Zelensky Calls for Meeting and Ceasefire

items.descriptionTR: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday rejected a proposal by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for a face-to-face meeting to end the four-year war, saying he saw "no point" in meeting his Ukrainian counterpart until a possible peace deal had been agreed. Read about the day’s events as they unfolded on our liveblog.
items.titleTR: Putin rules out Zelensky's offer to meet and vows to pursue war goals

items.titleTR: Armenia: Moscow, Meddling & the Mountain

items.titleTR: Western Balkan leaders join EU summit amid renewed enlargement drive

items.descriptionTR: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that Europe faced what he called an invasion of dangerous ideologies arriving by sea, linking immigration to the legacy of the D-Day landings in remarks in Normandy.
items.titleTR: Europe faces 'invasion' of dangerous ideologies - Hegseth

items.descriptionTR: Le secrétaire américain de la Défense a évoqué samedi 6 juin une «invasion» d’immigrés en commémorant le Débarquement de juin 1944, tout en appelant les pays européens à augmenter leurs capacités militaires.
items.titleTR: Sur les plages du Débarquement, Pete Hegseth tente un parallèle douteux entre l’immigration et la Seconde guerre mondiale

items.descriptionTR: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan's government has been accused by the West of abuses including unlawful killings and mass detentions.
items.titleTR: Tanzania President Visits Russia as Western Ties Fray

items.descriptionTR: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan begins a three-day state visit to Russia on Wednesday – the first official trip by a Tanzanian head of state to Moscow since 1969 – as her government faces growing criticism from Western countries over violence linked to the country's 2025 elections.
items.titleTR: Tanzania's Hassan makes historic Russia visit amid frayed ties with West

items.descriptionTR: Rights advocates and researchers are highlighting mounting political indoctrination and criminal prosecution facing children in Russia.
items.titleTR: The Kids Aren’t Alright: Rights Groups Warn of Mounting Pressure on Children in Russia

items.descriptionTR: It is the moving story of a Russian father and daughter who opposed Vladimir Putin’s war in Ukraine. It all began in March 2022, when 12-year-old Maria drew an anti-war picture at school in response to the invasion launched a month earlier. She was immediately reported by those around her, and the FSB soon visited both her school and her home. Her father was eventually arrested for supporting his daughter and speaking out against the war. He was convicted of discrediting the Russian army. Following his release from a penal colony, he and Maria left Russia and are now refugees in Strasbourg. A report by Elena Volochine, English adaptation by Lauren Bain.
items.titleTR: Exiled for an anti-war drawing: A Russian family punished for dissent

items.descriptionTR: European Council President Antonio Costa said new ways need to be found to speed up Western Balkans membership in the EU. His comments come ahead of an upcoming summit in Montenegro.
items.titleTR: EU seeking ways to speed up Western Balkans membership

items.descriptionTR: The European Union has reached a deal on tougher migration rules that would allow countries to set up so-called “return hubs” outside the bloc, a move hailed by supporters as a practical answer to stalled deportations, but denounced by rights groups as a dangerous step towards offshore detention. Meanwhile, the question of EU enlargement is also on the cards at a Western Balkans summit.
items.titleTR: EU tightens migration rules, eyes strategic enlargement in Balkans

items.descriptionTR: Prime Minister Peter Magyar and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced a deal that could free up over €16 billion in EU funds for Hungary. Now, Magyar's new government needs to deliver.
items.titleTR: What Hungary must do to receive EU funds frozen under Orban

items.descriptionTR: Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar meets French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace on Wednesday, as the two leaders look to strengthen European support for Ukraine following the end of Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule.
items.titleTR: Macron to meet Hungary's PM Magyar to discuss Ukraine, European defence

items.descriptionTR: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has urged European countries to confront what he described as an “invasion” of their coastlines by migration, using a D-Day anniversary speech in Normandy to press both cultural and security arguments central to President Donald Trump’s administration.
items.titleTR: Hegseth urges Europe to counter migrant 'invasion' in D-Day anniversary speech

items.descriptionTR: US Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth on Saturday marked the 82nd anniversary of the World War II D-Day landings in France with a speech that bemoaned the "invasion" of "boats and men" on Europe's beaches. In his address at a US military cemetery in Normandy, Hegseth also called on allies to contribute more to their defence.
items.titleTR: Hegseth blasts ‘invasion’ of migrants on Europe’s beaches in D-Day speech in France

items.titleTR: Ukraine war and risk of stagnation hang over St Petersburg economic conference

items.titleTR: El Nino threat grows as Europe prepares for another hot summer
